html:
The Dawn Raids were police raids in New Zealand in the mid 1970s on the homes of Pacific Islanders accused of staying past the end of their visas.

In the 1950s and 1960s New Zealand's factories needed workers, and many people came from Samoa, Tonga and Fiji. When the economy turned down after the 1973 oil shock, overstayers became a political target. Police burst into homes early in the morning or late at night, and stopped people in the street who looked Polynesian and asked for papers. Raids began under the Labour government in 1974 and grew harsher under Robert Muldoon's National government from 1976.

Pacific Islanders were only a minority of overstayers, many of whom came from Britain or North America, yet they made up most of those prosecuted. The raids hurt Pacific communities deeply and helped spark activism such as the Polynesian Panthers.

In 2021 Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern made a formal government apology for the raids.
sum: The Dawn Raids were police raids in New Zealand in the mid 1970s on the homes of Pacific Islanders accused of staying past the end of their visas.
